title: Quantifying Focused Ion Beam Milling Damage During Cryo-lamella Preparation
content: The application of focused ion beam (FIB) milling to frozen hydrated cells has made it possible to visualize thick cells and tissues with cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) at near atomic resolutions [1,2]. Cryogenic FIB-milling lacks the large scale distortions that characterized previous approaches, but retains a variable layer of damage from the milling process. We recently demonstrated that standard protocols for Gallium liquid metal ion source (LMIS) FIB-milling generate a variable layer of damage extending ∼60 nm from each lamella surface [3]. Milling using plasma ion sources, such as Argon and Xenon, have been presented as alternatives [4,5], but instrumentation is costly and inaccessible to many users, and we lack a direct comparison of their relative damage. We therefore sought to directly compare FIB-milling damage from different ions and accelerating voltages. We show that ion and acceleration voltage choice cause a detectable change in the damage layer of a lamella. We identify conditions that reduce lamella damage, improve particle detection and increase signal in resulting lamellae. In a rapidly growing field, a quantitative understanding of different FIB approaches and protocols to balance lamella thickness and FIB-milling damage are essential for informed decisions regarding their use.
